key_facts: No history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
No significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
Normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium are consistent with an ostium secundum atrial septal defect.

rejected.label: Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
rejected.why: Typically associated with anomalous pulmonary venous return, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: Usually presents with additional findings such as mitral or tricuspid regurgitation, which are not described

rejected.label: Ostium Primum Atrial Septal Defect
rejected.why: Often associated with other cardiac anomalies, such as mitral valve abnormalities, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Patent Foramen Ovale
rejected.why: Typically smaller and not associated with significant left-to-right shunting or chamber dilation
